kill_fact: The asymmetry itself survives primary-source attack, but the file's DECISIVE bear pillar is contractually false. The dossier states in five separate places that the automatic extension right is 'spent' / 'exhausted', so that any third deadline requires Zijin to affirmatively re-commit to a January price - this is the load-bearing reason the 29 July date is framed as a forcing event and the reason the break branch carries 45% weight. The Arrangement Agreement, as disclosed in Allied's own special-meeting circular dated 25 February 2026, defines the Outside Date as 29 May 2026, 'provided that ... such date shall be automatically extended by two months on UP TO TWO OCCASIONS'. May 29 -> July 29 consumed the FIRST occasion. A second automatic two-month extension to approximately 29 September 2026 is available on the face of the contract, conditional only on the regulatory condition (s.6.1(d)) being the unsatisfied one, no Key Regulatory Approval having been denied by non-appealable decision, and no breach by the extending party. The company's 29 May press-release gloss ('any further extension will require the parties' mutual agreement') conflicts with the agreement text and was adopted by the dossier without ever checking the underlying document. Consequence: the single most likely 29 July outcome is a near-mechanical slip to late September that resolves nothing and carries no information about buyer resolve - the opposite of the file's reading that a third extension 'would itself carry information'. The catalyst is materially SOFTER as a forcing function than even the file's SOFT_EXTENDED label conveys, while the deal is somewhat MORE alive than the 45% break weight implies. Verified intact: C$44.00 cash consideration, 27% premium to 30-trading-day VWAP, approximately C$5.5bn, 126,547,893 shares outstanding, ICA/ECOWAS/COMESA clearances, outstanding PRC approvals, and a live spread (US$20.85 vs approximately US$31.17). Floor remains soft but the file says so explicitly, and the buyer's walk-away does appear free: the only disclosed break fee, the C$220,000,000 Termination Amount, is payable BY ALLIED to Zijin, with no reverse termination fee payable by the purchaser found anywhere in the circular.
corrections: 1) MATERIAL - 'the automatic extension right is spent / exhausted; a third deadline requires Zijin's active consent' is WRONG. The Arrangement Agreement (circular dated 25 Feb 2026) provides automatic two-month extension 'on up to two occasions'; only one has been used. A second automatic extension to approximately 29 Sept 2026 is available. Fix the dated_milestone, bear_thesis, forcing_function and moderator_conclusion, and re-weight: the break-at-deadline branch is overweighted and the 'third extension is a fresh Zijin decision' inference is unsupported. 2) MATERIAL - 'Since 10 June there has been no such statement from either side' and the entire 'silence is itself information' hidden-signal is FALSIFIED. Allied furnished a 6-K on 17 July 2026 attaching a Management Information Circular board-approved 29 June 2026. The file's most recent company source is 10 June; it missed a filing eleven days before its own asserted verification date. 3) MATERIAL/NEW - that 17 July filing calls an ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING for 7 August 2026 (record date 7 July 2026, virtual), nine days AFTER the outside date, stating: 'If the transaction with Zijin Gold closes prior to, or on or about August 7, 2026, the annual general meeting will be cancelled.' The board was formally provisioning for a post-29-July world by 29 June, before the 21 July trade report the file treats as its decisive disclosure. This is far harder evidence for the file's own 'board preparing for independence' inference than the 10 June release it cites, and it independently corroborates that closing by 29 July was never the working assumption. 4) MODERATE - the outstanding Chinese gate is not a single NDRC decision. The circular defines 'PRC Approvals' as approvals from the NDRC, the Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) AND the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE); 'Purchaser Governmental Approvals' additionally requires the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. More gates than the file's single-regulator framing, though NDRC is plausibly the binding one. 5) MINOR/OMISSION - the file never mentions the C$220,000,000 Termination Amount payable by Allied to Zijin in certain circumstances (approximately C$1.74/share, approximately US$1.23/share). It does not break the floor and it is not a reverse fee, but it is a disclosed deal term absent from a file that explicitly reasons about break economics. 6) MINOR - premium basis is the 30-trading-day VWAP, not a '30-day average price'. 7) UNVERIFIED, NOT REFUTED - the Ethiopian approval 'around 14 July 2026' and the 21 July 2026 trade report (NDRC weighing Mali security and the premium; Zijin IR declining timing guidance) could NOT be independently confirmed against any primary source; neither appears in any SEC filing. The 21 July report is the sole basis for the file's claim that the regulator's objection is economic rather than procedural - the pillar that drives the whole 'time is against the holder' thesis. Treat as single-sourced trade press, not established fact. 8) CONFIRMED, NOT A CORRECTION - the buyer's exit does appear costless; no reverse termination fee payable by Zijin appears anywhere in the arrangement circular.
evidence: Allied Gold Corporation, Notice and Management Information Circular for the Special Meeting re Plan of Arrangement with Zijin Gold International, dated 25 February 2026 (furnished on Form 6-K, SEC EDGAR CIK 0001993344, accepted 9 March 2026). Defines 'Outside Date' as 29 May 2026 'provided that ... such date shall be automatically extended by two months on up to two occasions'; 'Consideration' means C$44.00 in cash per Common Share, a premium of approximately 27% on the 30 trading-day VWAP, approximately C$5.5 billion aggregate; 'Termination Amount' means C$220,000,000, payable by Allied to the Purchaser in certain circumstances; 'PRC Approvals' means approvals from the NDRC, MOFCOM and SAFE. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1993344/000110465926025078/tm266378d3_ex99-1.htm

Allied Gold Corporation press release dated 29 May 2026, Exhibit 99.1 to Form 6-K (SEC accepted 29 May 2026): Investment Canada Act approval received, completing the Canadian approval process; merger clearance received from the ECOWAS Regional Competition Authority and from COMESA; 'the Outside Date ... has been extended to July 29, 2026 in accordance with the Arrangement Agreement. Any further extension of the Outside Date will require the parties' mutual agreement.' Also discloses agreed amendments to the Credit Facility with implementation 'in progress', and never names the outstanding approval. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1993344/000117184326003808/exh_991.htm
